_readme: The kinds of clue to the director's note that the human's card shows (T88). BPC_NoteClue on BP_Show reads this file once per run. At each Scene Prep it draws one kind this show hasn't used: scene 1 draws only among kinds with scene_1 true (today only category), and every later scene among all unused kinds, so no kind repeats in a show. Local/switches.json's clue forces one kind by its id, in every scene.

id: the kind's id, which the log and the state use. label: the card's name for it ('Clue: <label>'). how: one line, sent to the AI actors as scene_card.note_clue.how, that says how the clue was made from the note. from: 'built' when BPC_NoteClue.Build makes the text from the note's words (and its key), or the name of the note's field in scenes.json that holds the text. prefix: text the clue starts with, on the card and in the state. mono: the card shows the text in the mono font, so a run of blanks can be counted.

The clue's text reaches the AI actors word for word as scene_card.note_clue.text, with kind and how. The input LLM never gets the note or the clue. Tools/check_prompts.py checks that this file holds the twelve kinds, that every 'from' that isn't 'built' is a field every note has, and that only category has scene_1 true.

kinds.label: Category
kinds.how: the note's category, one word that says what kind of thing the note is about

kinds.label: Vowels only
kinds.how: the note with every letter except a, e, i, o and u turned into _; spaces and punctuation kept

kinds.label: First letters
kinds.how: the first letter of each word of the note, then …, with each word's punctuation kept

kinds.label: Consonants only
kinds.how: the note with a, e, i, o and u turned into _

kinds.label: Scrambled words
kinds.how: the note with the letters of each word shuffled in place; word order and punctuation kept

kinds.label: Pig Latin
kinds.how: the note in Pig Latin: each word's leading consonants moved to its end plus ay, or yay after a word that starts with a vowel

kinds.label: Key word hidden
kinds.how: the whole note with its one key word blacked out, one block per letter

kinds.label: Only the key word
kinds.how: the note with every word blacked out except its one key word, one block per letter

kinds.label: Emoji
kinds.how: two to four emoji written to stand for the note

kinds.label: Opposite day
kinds.how: the reverse of the note's rule; the human must do the opposite of it

kinds.label: Director's riddle
kinds.how: a riddle of at most 10 words in the director's voice that hints at the note without its key word

kinds.label: Autocorrect
kinds.how: the note with two or three words swapped for words spelled almost the same
